title: He looked anointed.
paragraphs: But heaven had already turned away.
And nobody in the crowd could see it.

Because you can look right…
and be wrong where it matters most.

You can carry the crown…
and still lose the heart.

Tall. Strong. Commanding.
The kind of man who made a nation feel secure just by standing there.
Scripture says, “There was not a man among the people of Israel more handsome than he. From his shoulders upward he was taller than any of the people” (1 Samuel 9:2).
And that was enough… for them.
Because Saul’s story is not just ancient history.
We know how to look right.
We know how to say the right words, post the right verses, raise the right hands in worship, smile at church, lead when people are watching.
Private fears that control public decisions.
Saul didn’t lose the kingdom overnight.
One act of partial obedience dressed up as “good enough.”
One moment of choosing people’s approval over God’s command.
Until finally, the truth came out.
“I was afraid of the people and so I gave in to them.” (1 Samuel 15:24)
The leader… led by the crowd.
Saul feared people more than he feared God.
And when fear of people sits on the throne of your heart… God does not.
Some of us are not walking in obedience because we’re still listening to the wrong voices.

“What will they think?”
“What will I lose?”
“What if I’m rejected?”
We manage sin instead of killing it.
And like Saul, we keep the image intact while the soul is collapsing.
Every moment we chose approval over obedience.
“Man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7)
God rejected Saul as king (1 Samuel 15:26).
But because his heart refused full obedience.
Some scholars interpret Saul’s rejection as a gradual spiritual hardening—a pattern of disobedience that revealed where his allegiance truly was.
And outward success can hide inward decay… for a while.
Because this is where grace breaks in.
Because if Saul’s story ended with rejection, we would all be in trouble.
But the Bible doesn’t just give us Saul.
Saul was chosen because he looked like a king.
Jesus came looking like anything but.
“He had no beauty or majesty to attract us to him… nothing in his appearance that we should desire him.” (Isaiah 53:2)
The true King didn’t arrive with height, armor, or outward impressiveness.
Where Saul grasped for approval, Jesus surrendered to the Father.

Where Saul said, “I feared the people,”
Jesus said, “Not my will, but yours be done.” (Luke 22:42)

Where Saul preserved his image,
Jesus gave up His life.
Jesus took the place of people like Saul.
Every moment you chose image over integrity…
Every time you feared people more than God…
Every hidden sin you thought nobody saw…
And still went to the cross.
“For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” (2 Corinthians 5:21)
Grace is not permission to stay the same.
Grace is the power to finally change.
You cannot hold onto your image and receive His transformation at the same time.
It must come into the light.
Because healing does not happen in hiding.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)
What fear is controlling your decisions?
What sin are you protecting because it costs too much to surrender?
God is not impressed by your image.
But He is ready to transform your heart.
Bring the real you before the real King.
Because the same God who rejected Saul’s disobedience…
welcomes every broken sinner who comes through Jesus.
